# Erdős Problem 63

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/63](https://www.erdosproblems.com/63)
- [dBEr51] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., *A colour problem for infinite graphs and a problem

- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.

- [Re24] Reiher, C., *Graphs of large girth*. arXiv:2403.13571 (2024).

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos63

/--
Does every graph with infinite chromatic number contain a cycle of length $2^n$ for infinitely
many $n$?

Conjectured by Mihók and Erdős. Solved affirmatively following the work of Liu and Montgomery
[LiMo20].

The linked formal proof (Codex) states the conclusion as `{n | HasCycleLength G (2 ^ n)}.Infinite`,
with `HasCycleLength G m` unfolding to `m ∈ G.cycleLengths`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos63.lean#L46"]
theorem erdos_63 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
        ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos63

reformulations.difference: The source says that cycles of length 2^n occur for infinitely many n. Lean expresses this as ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A subset S of ℕ is infinite exactly when it has an element at or above every natural-number bound: a finite set is bounded, and a bounded subset of ℕ is finite. Apply this to S = {n | 2 ^ n ∈ G.cycleLengths}. The full statement equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem theorem. The linked proof's HasCycleLength predicate was also checked to be definitionally the same as membership in G.cycleLengths.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the question, and answer(True), research solved, and the formal_proof record are supported. The exact linked proof and its dependencies rebuilt successfully in the scratch directory; #print axioms returned only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary checks confirmed that empty/finite graphs cannot satisfy the hypothesis, the complete graph on ℕ does satisfy it, and cycle lengths below 3 are excluded. The live erdosproblems.com/63 page was inaccessible because of Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the exact question was independently verified in Erdős (1984), p. 121, and the status was corroborated by Liu–Montgomery, the community database, and the verified formal proof.
